text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"Berkeley, CA","level":"city","category":"algorithmic_rent_setting","status":"pending","title":"Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63: Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels","requirement":"It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. It is also unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels. A coordinated pricing algorithm is a process that uses non-public Competitor Data (less than 90 days old) to calculate and recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms for future leases, in coordination between one Berkeley landlord and one or more of its competitors, including through a third-party vendor. Each month a violation continues, and each dwelling unit for which the algorithm was used, is a separate violation. The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution or return of illegal profits, and civil penalties, with attorney's fees awarded if the City prevails. An aggrieved tenant may sue for injunctive relief, money damages and civil penalties, with attorney's fees awarded if the tenant prevails. Lease provisions limiting a prevailing tenant's attorney's fees are unenforceable against such claims.","key_value":"Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; Competitor Data means non-public data less than 90 days old","coverage_conditions":"All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley and their landlords.
